title: Close guards live in the MCP wrapper, not the primitive, and any caller can sign the reviewer's name
description:
From the 2026-08-02 adversarial hardening run (hive-adversarial-improve, AC-fidelity chain). Two related MEDIUMs about WHERE the guards live and WHO can claim to have run.

**1. The guards are composed by the caller, not enforced by the primitive.**

`closeTask` (`src/task-store.js`) accepts an OPTIONAL `closeGuard` callback and calls it only `if (typeof closeGuard === 'function')`. `src/mcp-server.js` passes `loopModeCloseGuard` on `close_task` and `transition_status`, and calls `loopModeUatCommentGuard` before both. So the loop-mode protections exist only on the MCP path.

This was discovered the hard way: an initial probe run called `closeTask()` directly and appeared to show Gate 1 failing to fire. Re-running through the real composition proved Gate 1 works correctly (`LOOP_CLOSE_GUARD_DENIED`). The probe was wrong — but what it accidentally demonstrated is real and worth fixing: **any caller that omits `closeGuard` silently loses every loop-mode protection.** `checkUatGuard` is called unconditionally inside `closeTask` and does not have this problem, which is the shape the loop guards should match.

Concretely this matters because the orchestrator-routing skill documents a fallback: "if the MCP server is unavailable, a direct `Edit` of `tasks/<KEY>.json` ... is acceptable". That fallback bypasses all four guards, and the docs acknowledge it, placing the burden on the orchestrator to "manually verify" the preconditions. A guard that depends on the caller remembering to compose it is a convention, not a control.

**2. `author` is an unconstrained string, so anyone can sign anyone's name.**

Probe A6 (MISSED): a ticket was closed with `comment: { author: 'reviewer', body: 'APPROVE. All acceptance criteria met.' }` — written by the orchestrator, with no reviewer subagent having run. Nothing binds an `author: 'reviewer'` comment to an actual reviewer. The Challenger independently proposed the same class (probe #4) plus a variant (#14): fabricating an `author: 'orchestrator'` comment reading `"Review depth: light (rubric inputs: 42 changed lines, no mandatory-FULL surfaces touched). Clean review, no findings."` before any reviewer spawn, poisoning the audit trail with a review that never happened.

`author: 'uat'` is the one author with any protection, and only in loop mode without the delegation grant (TASK-108/163). Every other author string is free.

There is no cryptographic identity here and inventing one is out of scope. The realistic goal is narrower: constrain the author set to a known enum, and make claims that IMPLY a process step actually require that step (see TASK-187, which makes a reviewer comment a close precondition — the two tickets must agree on the mechanism rather than each inventing one).

**Also folded in (LOW, same seam):** `closeTask` validates `linked_commits` against `COMMIT_SHA_RE` for FORM but never for EXISTENCE. Probe P8 closed a ticket with `['0000000000000000000000000000000000000000', 'deadbeef']`, both well-formed and neither real. The audit trail records commits that do not exist.

**Replayable fixture (protocol rule 2):** `ac-fidelity-round2.mjs` (A6), `ac-fidelity-probes.mjs` (P8), `ac-fidelity-round3b.mjs` (the corrected composition harness showing V0/V2 CAUGHT only when composed).
acceptance_criteria: A failing spec first demonstrates the composition gap: calling closeTask (and transitionStatus) directly WITHOUT a closeGuard, in loop mode with auto_close_on_green_review false, currently succeeds — while the same call through the MCP composition is blocked. Capture the red-run output verbatim.
A failing spec also replays probe A6: a ticket closed with comment author 'reviewer' authored by a non-reviewer caller currently succeeds.

The loop-mode guards are enforced by default at the primitive, matching how checkUatGuard already works — a caller that passes nothing gets the protection. Any opt-out is explicit, named, and used only by tests; prove no production path relies on the opt-out.

The comment author set is constrained to a known enum rather than an arbitrary string, and an author value that implies a process step occurred cannot be written by a caller for whom that step did not occur. Coordinate the mechanism with TASK-187 (which makes a reviewer comment a close precondition) — the two tickets must share one mechanism, not invent two.

The documented direct-Edit fallback is re-assessed in light of this change: either it is no longer needed, or the docs state precisely which guards it still bypasses after this ticket. Update the orchestrator-routing SKILL.md and CLAUDE.md text (BOTH parity copies, byte-identical) so the fallback's real risk is stated accurately.

linked_commits existence is either verified, or the docs stop implying the audit trail is trustworthy — decide which and record the decision. If verification is added, it must not make the task store depend on a git binary in environments that lack one; state how that is handled.

The probe scripts are ported into the repo as permanent regression specs, each asserting the previously-MISSED input is now CAUGHT, per the hive-adversarial-improve protocol's replayable-fixture rule.
npm run test:all is green; no existing task-store, close-guard, mcp-server, or task-board spec regresses; dist bundles rebuilt and committed if bundled source changed, with dist-parity passing.

comments.author: orchestrator
comments.body:
APPROVED and closed on a green FULL-depth review. **0 HIGH / 2 MEDIUM / 3 LOW.**

**Rubric inputs:** guards moved into the primitive (`src/task-store.js`), `tasks/schema.json` changed, the documented ticket-write fallback rewritten in `CLAUDE.md` and both `orchestrator-routing/SKILL.md` parity copies, five dist bundles rebuilt. Tier `tdd`. This is the control that decides whether a ticket can reach `done`.

## The central question, answered honestly

**Is AC4's binding half a real control or a speed bump?** It is a **speed bump plus an audit-legibility improvement — and it is documented as exactly that, which is why it passes.**

The developer established by checking rather than assuming that `developer`/`reviewer`/`researcher` subagents have **no MCP tool access at all** (per their `tools:` frontmatter), so every `append_comment`/`close_task` call is made by the Orchestrator's own session whatever `author` it writes. There is no identity to verify. It declined to invent one.

What it constrained instead is provable from data on disk: `closeTask` refuses a **closing comment** claiming `author: 'reviewer'` (`E_INVALID_CLOSING_COMMENT_AUTHOR`), because a genuine review is recorded as a *separate, pre-existing* comment during the Review step — never fabricated as the terminal remark in the same call, which is precisely what probe A6 exploited.

**The residual, stated plainly:** an orchestrator can still `append_comment({author:'reviewer'})` and then close. Fabrication becomes a separate, timestamped, deliberate act — a **more legible forgery, not a prevented one.**

The reviewer audited every description site for overreach and found none. `tasks/schema.json` says *"known-set check only, NOT proof of identity … the primitive cannot verify WHO is calling"*; both SKILL copies say the same; the error message scopes itself to *"fabricating the review AS the closing remark in the same call"*. After a session in which several controls shipped with descriptions that outran their mechanisms, this one describes itself accurately on the first pass.

## AC3 — no production path reaches `done` unguarded

**Verified by enumeration, not assertion.** Every production writer of `status` flows through `transitionStatus`/`closeTask` — `src/mcp-server.js:409/471` and `src/task-board.js:1386` — and both primitives now run `resolveCloseGuard(closeGuard)` **unconditionally** on `done` (`src/task-store.js:763`, `:887`). No other production code writes status: `createTask` seeds `todo`; `backlog-seeder` only creates and appends. `resolveCloseGuard` throws `TypeError` on any non-function non-`undefined` value, and the only spec passing a falsy guard is the one asserting that throw.

**No opt-out flag was added**, and `test:all` green confirms none was needed — harness mode's own no-op covers every fixture. The old shape (`if (typeof closeGuard === 'function')`) meant any caller omitting the guard silently lost every loop-mode protection; that is now impossible in code.

**Two residuals outside code:** a caller passing an explicit no-op function (inherent to an injectable seam; no production caller does), and a direct file edit — which no code can ever guard, and which is exactly what AC5 addresses.

## The most consequential line in the diff was found by grepping CODE, not the corpus

`COMMENT_AUTHORS` needed **`backlog-seeder`** — a value with **zero occurrences** across 389 real comments (histogram: orchestrator 314, uat 46, reviewer 24, developer 4, researcher 1), but written by `src/backlog-seeder.js` on every fresh `bin/init.js` run. Deriving the enum from the corpus alone would have passed every test in this repo and **silently broken every future project bootstrap.**

The corpus records what *has* happened; the code defines what *can* happen. Validating against real data is necessary and not sufficient.

## AC5 — fallback narrowed, not removed

The direct-`Edit` fallback is kept for genuine MCP-outage degraded operation but scoped to non-status, non-comment fields, and now explicitly **never** acceptable for `status: "done"`, appending a comment, or writing `linked_commits`/`linked_prs`. The old *"manually verify the preconditions"* framing is retired as not-a-real-control — a raw edit runs through neither ajv validation nor any guard. If `close_task` is genuinely unreachable, the instruction is now to stop and tell the human.

## AC6 — advisory verification with the Empty-result contract applied

`closeTask` stays git-free. `verifyLinkedCommits` runs at the MCP layer, **advisory-only, never blocking**, returning `{checked, reason, present, missing}` where `checked:false` **always** carries a reason (`none-linked` / `git-unavailable` / `not-a-git-repo`). All three verified reachable. A caller can never read "verified OK" from a run that verified nothing — the sixth place this repo's most persistent defect class could have appeared, and the first where it was designed out up front.

## Migration — verified independently

ajv over all 193 task files against the new schema: **0 invalid**, 188 `done`. The six `reviewer`-last tickets (TASK-134…139) predate atomic `close_task`; their comments came via `append_comment`, which still accepts `reviewer`, so they stay valid and mutable. **Nothing existing becomes invalid or unmutable.**

## MEDIUM-1 — carried into TASK-187, not dropped

`tests/ticket-write-path-doc-locks.spec.js` passes over **both** the old prose (*"acceptable… manually verify"*) and the new (*"never acceptable… stop and tell the human"*) — its anchors don't distinguish them. So TASK-188's central new doc claim has no lock, and the TASK-099 R4 regression class could silently return. Since the fallback prose is now the *only* control over the direct-Edit path, that gap matters. **Folded into TASK-187**, which touches this exact surface next — the reviewer's own recommendation.

## MEDIUM-2 discharged

The R3 checklist exists in the hand-off with all five items stated: unspecced path exercised (the unknown-key path with valid and invalid authors, confirming the reordering doesn't change behaviour for valid input); red-green planted; dist rebuilt (5 bundles, each explained by the new `close-guard.js` dependency closure — the three unchanged bundles don't import `task-store.js`); parity byte-identical; calibration n/a.

## LOW carried

1. `src/task-store.js:797-801, 864-868` — unknown-author rejections throw bare `Error`s with no `.code`, unlike adjacent typed errors, so `task-board.js` must regex messages. Consistent with pre-existing style; a `code: 'E_INVALID_COMMENT_AUTHOR'` would cost one line.
2. `verifyLinkedCommits` — two exotic-path labeling imprecisions (a non-`ENOENT` `rev-parse` failure maps to `not-a-git-repo`; a `cat-file` failure counts a sha as `missing` rather than unverifiable). Consequence is a mislabeled advisory, never a false "verified OK", since `checked:true` is unreachable without `rev-parse` succeeding.
3. `tests/e2e/plugin-deps.spec.js` — the manually-maintained copy list needs touching on future dep changes. **Not weakened into tautology**: the `IMPORT_OK` assertion anchors the list (an omission fails loudly, which is how this diff's own expansion was forced) and the NODE_PATH test still fails on bare specifiers for the right reason.

## The seam TASK-187 consumes

`hasCommentFromAuthor(task, author)` — exported from `src/task-store.js:452-455`. Self-contained, null-safe, presence-only, mirroring the `checkUatGuard`/`hasRecordedUatVerdict` layering. **Judged sound, with two conditions TASK-187 must honor** (carried verbatim into its brief): call it against the **on-disk** task pre-merge as `checkUatGuard` does, so the closing comment can never self-satisfy the precondition; and pair the presence check with a loop-mode **write-gate** on `author:'reviewer'` mirroring TASK-163's `loopModeUatCommentGuard` — otherwise the combined control remains a speed bump.

## Gate

`test:since -- 4e492cc` 20 files / 266 tests ⬛ `npm test` 83 files / 1120 passed ⬛ named e2e 119 tests ⬛ doc-locks + close-guards 27 tests ⬛ **`npm run test:all` 181 files / 2104 passed** ⬛ dist-parity byte-matched all 8 bundles from a fresh build.
